minutes.headline: Capital Planning heard police, fire and DPW 10-year plans; no votes beyond adjournment, prioritization starts Nov 21.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the last three department capital presentations (police, fire, DPW). Discussion centered on vehicle fleet aging, ambulance and radio infrastructure, DPW truck failures, bundling items under the capital threshold, the Cortland Circle drainage project lacking a plan, and cemetery items that might belong in the operating budget. No substantive votes; the committee will begin prioritization at its next meeting.

public_comment.topic: Resident asked presenters to say how much big-ticket items like fire trucks, ambulances and DPW trucks rise in cost annually if purchases are delayed.

votes.outcome: passed; roll call of aye votes from Martin, Brunner, passios, beardmore and chair

budget_items.what_was_said: Police have no capital request for the next fiscal year; a 10-year plan of regular cruiser, radio and vest replacements was presented, with cruiser life extended through rotation.
Vehicle for school resource officer and firearms replacement were listed.
Fire chief figures about five percent annual increase on apparatus, ambulances at least ten percent, with some quotes much higher.
Also submitted under ARPA funding; maintenance costs discussed including one costly engine overhaul year.
Phase two cost assumed as phase one plus a percentage for price increases.
Government insurers set rates, making up most of billed transports; ambulance revenue goes to the general fund and will not become an enterprise fund.
DPW director spread equipment requests roughly evenly per year.
Members questioned bundling catch basin equipment items that individually fall under the capital threshold.
A drainage request was questioned for lacking an engineered plan or place to discharge water.
Hedges, turf, headstone restoration and plot survey were bundled; members suggested two go in the operating budget.
Perpetual care is a small per-plot amount covering basic care, and DPW gets a small annual purchase of services amount for tree and hedge work.

decisions.decision: Committee to begin prioritizing capital requests at the next meeting, with the list due to the town manager by about December 15.
Next meeting set for Monday November 21, 6 pm, with two to three more meetings expected to finalize the list.
DPW director noted the bundling concern for future capital submissions.
DPW director to share his DPW vehicle inventory; town manager suggested posting it publicly.
Police chief to provide a visual fleet timeline for future presentations.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee heard the last three departmental 10-year capital plans: police, fire and public works.
Police reported no capital request for the next fiscal year and presented a ten-year plan of cruiser, radio and vest replacements.
Members questioned bundling catch basin equipment under the capital threshold and a drainage request with no engineered plan or discharge point.
Members suggested two of the bundled cemetery items belong in the operating budget rather than the capital plan.
The committee will begin prioritizing requests at its next meeting, with a list due to the town manager around mid-December; the only vote was to adjourn.

why_it_matters: These plans feed the capital list the town manager receives, which shapes what residents may later be asked to vote on at Town Meeting and how much goes into the tax levy.
How items are bundled, or moved between the capital and operating budgets, changes which spending is reviewed as capital and which competes with services in the operating budget.
